I was ordered by Shi Gu to draw the Jianmen Gate, and I made a note of it, and I playfully inscribed what I saw when I was traveling, and this is about it." Inscriptions: "Shou" in vermilion and "Zhengshu" in white.　　The year "Gengxu" is the ninth year of the Kangxi era (1670) of the Qing Dynasty, when Yun Shouping was 38 years old.　　The title indicates that Yun Shouping and his friends, Wang Shigu and Lu Han, who were also good at painting, were both traveling to Jianmen in Mount Yu, and were so impressed by the steepness of the mountain that Yun Shouping was asked by Wang Shigu to record the trip in the form of a painting, making this one of the most authentic drawings of the landscape of Jianmen in Mount Yu.　　The painting is small in size, and instead of painting from the foot of the mountain, the author has painted only a portion of the wall in order to show the momentum of the Jianmen stone wall as it "rises into the air," leaving the top and foot of the mountain omitted to give more room for the imagination to reach up and bottom out. At the same time, the author uses the artistic technique of comparison to paint the manners of his friend and his friend visiting the cliff in the picture, thus setting off the towering cliff of the mountain. The rocks in the painting are painted with a bright and elegant color scheme, and the brushwork is loose and elegant, revealing Yun Shouping's characteristic of a landscape painting with a sense of spirituality and clarity.
